reports.title: Toledo Bend bass will relate heavily to grass and channel edges this month
reports.text:
This young angler caught a chunky Toledo Bend bass on a trip with Living the Dream Guide Service’s Matthew Loetscher.
There’s more bass habitat, i.e. good ol’ hydrilla, now in Toledo Bend than in more than a decade, which is sweet, welcome news for the fish and bass anglers.
We haven’t had grass like this in a long time. Where it traditionally grew 10 years ago, it’s growing again. There are lots of areas where we’ve got matted hydrilla out to 8, maybe 15 feet deep in some places.
And with the seasonal cooldown that brings lower water temperatures, that grass is giving up bass via topwaters — buzz baits and plastic frogs — and punchin’ right now. It’s about as close to the good old days as…
